decisions.reason: Although the firm has already invested in and publicly presented it, the superfood drink mix sits less centrally in its long-term industrial waste-and-energy technology direction, so management is relatively likely to reallocate resources despite some commitment pressure.

These modular waste-to-energy extensions fit the firm’s core engineering and deployment business, and even with only limited website visibility management can justify continuing on the basis of prior development effort and slow industrial sales cycles.
The waste-oil-to-energy plant received a clear standalone launch and strong public framing, making sunk costs, reputational commitment and strategic fit all push management toward persistence.

The plastic-waste-to-fuel plant is close to the firm’s stated mission and was visibly promoted, so management is more likely to continue and attribute any weaker performance to temporary commercialization and regulatory conditions than to abandon it quickly.
